result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both screenshots show only the top of the page, so I couldn't see five full questions, the submit button or the results state in either one; I scored those items as roughly neutral. Both have plausible safety questions with no authoritative made-up figures: B's 2,500 lb scenario is clearly hypothetical and its 5 mph speed is hedged as 'commonly', while A avoids numbers entirely. A looks cleaner and more polished, whereas B's question headings sit on top of the card borders, which looks broken. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both pages show a plain, on-topic quiz with plausible safety questions, but each screenshot shows only the first questions, so the results state and missing-answer handling can't be checked for either. A's question headings (fieldset legends) overlap the card borders, which looks broken. It also mentions a 5 mph limit, though it hedges this as 'commonly' and defers to the posted site limit. B's layout is cleaner, with tidy option rows and no invented figures.
